claims.claim: Michael Dirda opens his review by quoting the first sentence of A Wizard of Earthsea, which names the island of Gont, its mile-high peak, its towns in high valleys and its ports on dark narrow bays before naming any person.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, "The Twilight of an Age of Magic" (review of Tehanu), The Washington Post, 25 February 1990
claims.quote: a single mountain that lifts its peak a mile above
claims.page: review opening, quoting A Wizard of Earthsea

claims.claim: Gerald Jonas, in the New York Times obituary, describes Le Guin’s fiction as combining compelling stories and rigorous narrative logic with a lean but lyrical style.
claims.source: Gerald Jonas, obituary of Ursula K. Le Guin, The New York Times, 23 January 2018

claims.claim: Gerald Jonas states that the first three Earthsea books, written for young adults at the publisher’s request, show no trace of writing down to their audience in scale or style.
claims.source: Gerald Jonas, obituary of Ursula K. Le Guin, The New York Times, 23 January 2018
claims.quote: elevated style betray no trace of writing down to an audience

claims.claim: Le Guin, quoted in her New York Times obituary, said she must find the right name for a character before she can get on with the story.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, quoted by Gerald Jonas, The New York Times obituary, 23 January 2018
claims.quote: I must find the right name or I cannot get on
claims.page: obituary body, paragraph on true names

claims.claim: Sean Guynes states that the tone of Le Guin’s writing in A Wizard of Earthsea is simpler and sparser than in The Left Hand of Darkness or The Dispossessed.
claims.source: Sean Guynes, "A Wizard of Earthsea: The Unsung Song of the Shadow", The Ursula K. Le Guin Reread, Tor.com, 8 April 2020
claims.quote: simpler and sparser than in The Left Hand of Darkness
claims.page: opening section of the reread instalment

claims.claim: Sylvia Kelso states that Le Guin, like Yeats, seems to move toward simplicity or at least austerity in the rhythm and content of her later work.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, "Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin", Paradoxa 21 (2009), pp. 7-22
claims.quote: Le Guin does seem to move toward simplicity

claims.claim: Sylvia Kelso states that Tehanu shows the skill of experience making less do more rather than more do more.
claims.source: Sylvia A. Kelso, "Boldly to Re-Venture: New Writing on the Works of Ursula K. Le Guin", Paradoxa 21 (2009), pp. 7-22
claims.quote: making less do more, rather than more do more

claims.claim: The frame narrator of 'The Matter of Seggri' opens the story in the past tense with a dated archival event rather than a scene.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: The first recorded contact with Seggri was in year 242

claims.claim: The Seggri frame records the killing of an observer by naming exactly what the record does not contain.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: disclosed the fact, but not the circumstances

claims.claim: The Seggri frame marks a gap in the archive with a present-tense statement that no record exists.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: There is no record of further contact with Seggri until
claims.page: frame passage after Captain Aolao-olao's report

claims.claim: The Seggri compiler uses a first-person-plural editorial voice that states the limit of its holding before excerpting a document.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: We have only her report, from which three excerpts follow.

claims.claim: A policy decision in the Seggri frame is reported as an agentless passive with the number written out in words.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: A limit of two hundred visitors from off world was set.

claims.claim: Each document in 'The Matter of Seggri' is introduced by a provenance line naming the kind of document, its recipient and its date.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: The following is a memoir given to Ambassador Eritho te Ves
claims.page: frame line before the Ush memoir

claims.claim: An observer's institutional advice is compressed in the Seggri frame into a nominalisation and two bare verbs.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: Her recommendation was to observe and avoid.

claims.claim: The Seggri frame reports a demographic figure in the present tense as a hedged ratio, giving the balance as about 12:1.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'The Matter of Seggri' (1994), full text transcription, sfsfss.com
claims.quote: the gender balance now stands at about 12:1
